title: How authority is built
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would make a stranger call you an authority?
A student said: make your brand stand out; if there are a hundred people with your name, use a middle name or initial, and stay consistent with whatever you decide.
Jose agreed: add a middle initial or something that separates you so you do not get lost in searches.
Jose said that you have to start writing in publications and putting out press releases, and that his team started doing interviews and co-branding with a trade magazine.
Jose said that your demeanor matters when they meet you after reading about you: your tone, purpose and style. Are you an aggressive businessperson or an empathetic servant leader?
He said to make a list of the people who influence you, because describing them reveals your own style.
Jose said he wants everyone to draw up a personal strategy, because if you do not do the work, we will only have talked about it. He said that he holds the group accountable as a teacher.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the version of your name you will use everywhere.
Write one publication you could write for.
Write your tone in three words.
Write your list of five people who influence you.
Write your personal strategy in five lines.

check.q: What did a student say to do with a crowded name?
choices: Use a middle name or initial

check.q: What did Jose say to start doing?
choices: Writing in publications and press releases

check.q: What did Jose say he does as a teacher?

recap: Stand out, get published, know your tone, do the work.
